title: 1000m Row Pacing
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: 1000m Row Pacing.

videos.description:
How to row your BEST 1000-meter row:

Having a goal will be a HUGE help if you’ve already done a 500m or a 2000m row before.

Basing a goal pace off of your 500m, aim for 3-9 split seconds slower than your 500m finish time. It’ll be closer to 7-9 seconds faster if you’re a dude, and closer to 3-5 seconds if you’re a gal!

Basing it off of your 2000m can be even more accurate. Take your 2000m row split/500m average and aim for 4-8 split seconds faster.

If you’re not sure how to calculate your 500m split average, google search “erg split calculator” and plug in the numbers!

If you don’t have anything to base your row off of, you just gotta keep in mind:

✅ Long strokes
✅ 26 strokes per minute or more
✅ Be conservative at the start
✅ Sprint the last 180m with all you’ve got!

Hopefully this helps! Good thing is… EVERYONE gets a personal best the first time 😉

How’d you do?? 👇

title: 2000 Meter Row Pacing
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for 2000 Meter Row Pacing.

videos.description:
For 99% of people, all you have to do to PR your 2000m row is to not start so fast.

TOO MANY let the adrenaline of the race get to them and end up burning out after the first 500m.

You HAVE to settle to a goal pace if you want to successfully pull a new best on the rower! And for the 2000m, that pace should feel ALMOST TOO EASY for the first 500m.

But then, if for SOME REASON you have extra energy in the last 500m, you can crank it up then! But you can’t get back burning out the first 500m…

To set your goal, go and search “erg split calculator”. Click on the link from @concept2inc and type in a finish time that is 1-2 seconds faster than your current record. All you have to do is SETTLE to that split and hold it after the first few strokes of the row.

Can YOU control your body and settle?

Or are you going to let another personal best slip away because you let adrenaline and ego get the best of you in the first 2 minutes?

The choice is yours.

videos.description:
✅ 2000m Row Strategy for your next PR!

Most people FAIL the 2k because they burn out the first 500 meters! You must remember that the 2000m row is like “the mile” 🏃‍♂️ of rowing! It’s actually LONGER than a mile!

And you don’t just SPRINT the start of a mile!! You pace yourself - and that’s what you’ve gotta do on this row!

Pacing yourself means finding a balance of stroke rate and power per stroke! You don’t want the rate too low - so aim for 26 SPM+ (32 SPM+ for the pros) while maintaining a MODERATE power output (NOT a max effort power per stroke)!

You do this, and the first 1000m might feel suspiciously easy! But that’s not a bad thing.. because you can always BRING MORE at the end, but you can’t get back burning the start! 🔥

If you want a true Personal Best / Personal Record (PR/PB), then use the Erg Pace Calculator (google it) to get you an accurate pace/500m to aim for based on your goal time!

Happy rowing! 🚣

title: 200m Row Sprint Strategy
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: 200m Row Sprint Strategy.

videos.description:
Here’s how I rowed a 24.5 sec 200m row:

I focused on 3 primary things in order to produce max power. Keep in mind, that this strategy ONLY WORKS for rows that are ~30 seconds or so. Anything longer than that and this type of rowing falls apart - so keep that in mind!!

First, I focus on a high stroke rate. In this video, my stroke rate is 60+. That is only sustainable for a few seconds, hence why I only go that high for a row like this. A row like 200m is too short to focus on long, strong strokes. Save those for 2000m rows!

Second, I focus on getting max power through the “lean and swing”. This means getting an exaggerated lean forward each stroke by only bending my legs just shy of 90 degree angles! This allows me to keep my heels down and lets me lean forward a lot - and then swing back with max power, too! This also helps to keep the stroke rate super high like I talked about earlier.

Third, I make sure to focus on a full leg extension each stroke. Because I’m bending my legs only a little bit, I need to make sure I’m getting the most out of them by trying to press them flat every stroke. Sometimes when trying to take fast strokes, we forget to actually straighten the legs and flex the quads each stroke!!

BONUS: sit heavy in the seat and make sure all of your effort is horizontal with no upwards pulling. If you pull up, even a little, you’ll fall off the seat (ouch).

That’s how I rowed a super fast 200m! How’s your 200m? Let me know down below! NOW, DO IT!

Love always,

title: 200m Row Sprint Technique
summary: Explains sprint-specific stroke length, handle height, heel position, and pacing for a 200-meter row.

videos.description: 🔥 Your BEST 200m sprint!  ✅ Heels planted, quick strokes! Can’t keep them down? You need to LEAN FORWARD more to prevent too much leg bend!  ✅ Keep your hands high! A shorter stroke means hands need to be a bit higher than usual!  ✅ Sit heavy and ONLY push and pull horizontally! The excitement of a short row can make you want to pull upwards, which will send you off of the seat!  🔥 GRIP AND RIP!!! You got this!! Now, do it!  Coach Austin 🤘 . . . #row #rowingmachine #rower #rowing #otf

⭐️ 200m TECHNIQUE! ⭐️ To SPRINT on the rower, you need to row differently than you would “normally”!

Short rows like 200m sprints take such a short amount of time, it is BETTER to take MORE strokes faster, rather than take long efficient strokes!

This means that to optimize your form:

1️⃣ Keep your heels planted. This allows you to take strokes quickly and with power!

2️⃣ Focus on your LEAN forward! The lean forward should have your torso on your thighs and arms stretched out. As you take strokes, drive your legs, and SWING back with power each stroke. Don’t forget to have some urgency to rush out and lean to the front again!

3️⃣ Lift your hands SLIGHTLY higher than normal. Handles are pulled out of rowing machines at a slight angle upwards, and because your stroke is shorter, you need to lift UP just a bit more than you think in order to feel strong and connected!

Do these things and you’ll be FAST! Don’t do them and you will be slow 🤷‍♂️ no matter how fit you think you are!

If you don’t believe me on any of this, go ahead and search “200m world record row” and watch all the attempts that use this EXACT formula!

title: 3 TIPS I USED FOR my PR 5:24 2000m row
summary: Covers pacing, progression, or workout-planning considerations for 3 TIPS I USED FOR my PR 5:24 2000m row.

videos.description:
3 TIPS I USED FOR my PR 5:24 2000m row!

1 - Remember that this is a LONG ROW no matter how fast or “slow” you are. This row is going to take 5 and a half minutes MINIMUM… for most, 7-9 minutes. Think about when you start the row really hard and fast… can you keep that for 7-9 minutes? OF COURSE YOU CAN’T SO DON’T DO THAT!

2 - Row long. You need as much LENGTH in each stroke as possible to keep you efficient for 7-9 minutes. Focus on the lean forward, bending your legs as much as you can. YES, YOUR HEELS CAN LIFT AND PROBABLY SHOULD! Heels planted is ideal for short intervals or if you have a large midsection that would prevent you from keeping your lean forward if you bent your legs more.

3 - Start off more conservative than you think you should. You can ALWAYS BRING MORE AT THE END but you CANNOT get back burning out the start! So don’t f*** yourself over by going crazy at the start because your adrenaline is high!

The first 500m should feel SUSPICIOUSLY EASY… Re-assess your pacing at the 1000m mark and THEN BRING MORE if you conserved too much. Most likely, you’ll have gone just hard enough to keep your pushing the same intensity for the rest of the row.

If you are immature and go really hard at the start, you’re gonna be f***ed for that final 500 meters - and that’s your own doing! I’M WARNING YOU NOW!!

BONUS TIP: THIS ROW IS GONNA BE HARD!! It’s going to be hard no matter what!! The sooner you accept that, the better mindset you’ll be able to cultivate to get after it and crush this row!! 

Good luck, get after it! NOW, DO IT!

3 Tips You NEED for Better Split Squats!

Tip 1 is to simplify your set up! Simply sit on your bench and extend your leg. Wherever your foot goes, that’s how far out it should be! Now, there is no more guessing if you are standing too close or too far.

Tip 2 is to NOT USE WEIGHTS... at least at first! That’s because MOST people who use weights right away don’t achieve the full range of motion! You want your knee to touch the ground at the bottom of each rep. If it’s not touching and you can’t get down there, you need to stop using weights and mastery the range with your bodyweight first! You have your whole life to use heavy dumbbells... so, do it RIGHT first!

Tip 3 is to think about “dropping the back knee down” in order to get the full range! If you only focus on “bending the front leg”, it’s going to feel awkward and you literally can’t get as down low as you need to!

I hope these 3 tips can help you out and make this exercise a little less daunting! Give them a try and let me know how it goes!

videos.description:
Why listen to some rando (me) when you can watch the WORLD RECORD HOLDER row the 500 meter row!?

When we watch @bigphil90 , his performance gives us great insight into a handful of useful techniques to do for this sprint row! Keep in mind, these techniques are specific to the 500m, and wouldn’t be advised for longer rows or any rowing focused on basic, steady-state cardio health & longevity.

This is form and technique for PERFORMANCE.

1️⃣ A focus on high stroke rate. Phil is 6 foot 9 inches tall, yet still manages a 40+ stroke rate throughout, managing a 47 in the last few pulls! ✅ Keep the stroke rate high, because this is a sprint!

2️⃣ Focus more on a BIG & STRONG lean and swing, rather than using long strokes. Check out Phil’s leg bend… it’s about 90 degrees. But that’s EXACTLY how much your legs should be bending to optimize power & stroke rate for this very niche sprint.

Bending your legs more will prevent the average person from getting the proper 11 o’clock lean forward you want for this sprint! So, try to think “90 degree leg bend”, which for most (not all) will be a “heels down” approach.

3️⃣ Fightint until the end! The effort and intensity from the first stroke to last stroke was virtually the same! And that’s because there was a goal race pace to hold (which you need to set and stick to) and an understanding that the last 150m will be UNBEARABLY HARD and you will want to slow down.

Fight until the end, even when your body wants to give in! What a row… 👏 Good luck to everyone sprinting their own 500m! Let me know how it goes! 💪 Now, do it!

videos.description:
YOUR BEST 500M FORMULA:

You must row “LONG AND STRONG” the entire way! This is a long sprint, so short choppy strokes are going to burn you out while you still have more to go!

To row LONG, you have to LEAN and SWING! That means you must get your shoulders in front of you at the front of the stroke. Then, push back and SWING into a “shoulders behind hips” position!

The hip swing is what keeps the watts high and keeps you going strong... DO NOT LET YOUR TORSO GO VERTICAL WHEN YOU ARE TIRED!!

At 200m to go, you will hit “The Wall”. No matter how fit you are, everyone hits it! You need to be aware of when it happens and be ready to FIGHT TO THE END!

In that last 150 meters, increase the stroke rate, keep the lean and swing, and don’t let your handle flow around... feed it STRAIGHT IN and OUT of the rower!

With all of this in mind, you’re going to dominate and crush the 500m! Good luck and let me know how your row goes!

Love always,

title: 500m Row Pacing and Sprint Technique
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: 500m Row Pacing and Sprint Technique.

videos.description:
How I rowed a 1:06 500 meter and howo row YOUR best 500 meter:

First, make sure you’re actually watching your split/500m when you row. This number will literally tell you, at your current intensity, how long your 500m will take. If you have a goal set, you need to get RIGHT TO THAT SPLIT TIME and hold it! If you don’t pay attention to it, you’re going into the unknown and are most likely just going to crash and burn on the row.

Second, it’s super important to  focus on quick, powerful strokes… because this thing is just a “sorta long sprint”. That means keeping your HEELS DOWN on the foot plates by bending your legs only to about 90 degrees and focusing mainly on getting a BIG LEAN FORWARD at the front of each stroke! If you don’t lean, you won’t be able to keep your heels down, so lean MORE than you think!

Third, you have to understand that no matter how fit you are, you will WANT TO BE NOT-ALIVE when you hit the last 150 meters or so. Physiologically, it’s your body’s break point. But you MUST keep going and not give into the fatigue. To keep your split as fast as possible, keep focusing on your BIG SWING forward and backwards. Don’t fall into the trap of “getting vertical” with your torso. That will be the end of you and you will NOT PR. KEEP LEANING AND SWINGING!!

Lastly, make sure you row THROUGH the finish line. Don’t stop with 5 meters left… you will regret it. You gotta take an EXTRA stroke more than you think to finish with your truly fastest time.
 Good luck! Let me know how your 500 meter row goes down below!

Love always,

summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Arnold-Press Continuous Rotation.

videos.description:
The Arnold Press is not what you think...

It’s not a step-by-step “turn and press” motion!

This exercise was designed originally to simply get more stretch on the shoulders by bringing the weights in front of you and down more. Whether or not it ACTUALLY stretches the shoulders more is up for debate, but that’s besides the point.

The point is, this motion is simply ONE MOTION! “Twist and press” at once, then reset. That’s literally it!

You will feel more fluid, strong, and in control when you can make it one motion of a “twist and press” rather than piecing it out.

Be sure to keep your chest nice and proud as you bring the weights in front to get as much shoulder stretch as you can and stabilize the press overhead.. you don’t wanna slouch on this one!! And I’m telling you this as a fellow sloucher tall guy!!

Hope this can clear the air a bit and makes sense. What are your thoughts on this exercise?

title: Bench Push-Up Progression
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: Bench Push-Up Progression.

videos.description:
Are you awful at pushups? It’s time to try this…

Bench Pushups are the secret sauce ingredient to get your STRONGER at your pushups to eventually finally do one on the ground without your knees.
 Regressing to the bench isn’t something to be embarrassed about - in fact quite the opposite! It shows that you don’t have an inflated ego getting in the way of you actually making progress!

With bench pushups, the SET UP can be TRICKY. You do not want to “stack your shoulders” or “stack your hips over your knees”. This will lead to reps that simply aren’t effective for your strength and improvement!

Instead, try to remember to have your shoulders “SLIGHTLY BEHIND” the hands and your knees “slightly behind” the hips. This ensures a strong plank position!

And as you do your reps, make sure you do NOT go “straight down”. Aim yourself “down and forward” to keep your shoulders healthy and maximally work your chest muscles!

As you get better at these, you can start doing bench pushups without your knees, then graduate to the ground on your knees, and with enough time and patience (a reminder that you have decades of life left), you’ll eventually knock out your first pushup without your knees!

Now, do it!

videos.description:
As we age, we slow down…

Or at least MOST do! But keeping up with power and athleticism is what helps keep us feeling young no matter our age! 💪 

The dumbbell Snatch is a GREAT way to work on this! But the problem is that it’s such an intimidating exercise for a lot of folks!

To get comfortable with a HEAVY weight going up and over our heads, try the “jump and zip” method!

The idea is to use the explosive power of our legs (which are much stronger than arms) to JUMP the weight up, and using that momentum, to “zip” the weight up like a big jacket! The “zip” keeps the weight close to your center of mass to keep you strong and stable!

title: Burpee Foot Placement
summary: Covers setup, common faults, and practical modifications for Burpee Foot Placement.

videos.description:
I seriously wouldn’t even BOTHER doing Burpees if you’re not going to take the time to GO WIDE with your feet.

Simply going up and down WITHOUT thinking about your feet placement brings more risk than rewards to this exercise - and I’d just pass it up.

When your feet aren’t wide, you’re simply forced to round your back as you go down, which is just asking for an accidental strain. (P.S. rounding your spine isn’t inherently BAD, but it is when you’re not intentionally trying to train spine rounding). It’s unathletic and isn’t going to make you better at anything. Plus, it’ll make you SLOWER, meaning you won’t be able to get in as many reps.

If you take the 0.1 seconds it takes to go WIDE with your feet, the risk of accidental injury goes down to practically ZERO! Wide feet allow you to squat down each rep - and that’s infinitely better than just rounding down each rep.

Think “Wide-Together-Wide” each rep! Your feet CAN come together but do it as you jump to the plank - NOT when you jump back up!

NOW DO IT!

Love always,

title: Burpee Technique for Speed or Strength
summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Burpee Technique for Speed or Strength.

videos.description:
Burpees “chest to floor”… to flop or not to flop?

Most would say flopping in and out of the pushup is ineffective… but honestly, CONTEXT matters!

If the goal is to get in reps quickly for competition, then flopping is 1000% going to be the fastest and most efficient way to get your reps done! But let’s be real: it’s not going to make you STRONGER or really help you make any gains outside of raising your heart rate.

If you want to use burpees to build STRENGTH and ATHLETICISM, you’ll need to slow things down a bit and take out the flop.

To make your burpees more effective, start by taking your feet wide! This makes it more effective to squat down and prevents back rounding and folding over each rep.

Then, for the pushup portion, try “knees on the ground” and aim down and slightly forward each rep to help you build actual strength in your pushups!

Which version is right for you? That’s for you to decide what’s important! Context matters!

Now do it!

title: Concentration Curl Wrist Position
summary: Explains how to keep the wrist neutral during concentration curls to maintain biceps tension and reduce elbow strain.

videos.description:
Your concentration curls shouldn’t become wrist curls!

A lot of people curl the dumbbell upward while simultaneously bending their wrist toward the body.

That can take tension away from the biceps and place more stress through the forearms and inner elbow.

Instead, keep your wrist slightly back.

Think: knuckles a little lower than the wrist.

This helps you achieve:

💪 More biceps
🤏 Less forearm involvement
✅ Better control

Don’t curl the wrist. Keep the tension where you actually want it! NOW DO IT!!
.
.
.
#biceps #bicepsworkout #concentrationcurls #armworkout #strengthtraining #exerciseform #gymtips #trainingtall

Concentration Curls are done wrong ~75% of the time!

When we isolate one arm at a time, with our elbow into the side of our leg as we curl up, the IMMENSE challenge of truly isolating the biceps TENDS to lead to MOST people curling up the wrist as they curl the weight up.

Curling your wrist is VERY BAD with this exercise and can lead to a Golfer’s Elbow injury over time if you do it repeatedly (this injury will keep you in pain for 6 months - 1 year)!

You HAVE to make sure you DO NOT curl your wrists as you curl the weight up. So, try to think “knuckles down” as you curl to keep your wrist relaxed and keep the action just in your biceps!

Hope that makes sense and you don’t WRITE IT OFF AS SOMETHING YOU DON’T DO!

After coaching 1000s of individuals through this movement over the years, MOST PEOPLE CURL THE WRISTS UNINTENTIONALLY! So, be intentional, and RELAX the wrist!

Love always,

Coach Austin 🤘

title: Controlling Rowing Intensity
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: Controlling Rowing Intensity.

videos.description:
💀 You’re dying on the rower because you’re treating it like a treadmill.

It’s like you’re pressing 15 mph, realizing you can’t, and then stop. You’d never do that while running - so you press a button that gives you a sustainable speed instead.

title: Cross Back Lunge Knee Safety
summary: Covers setup, common faults, and practical modifications for Cross Back Lunge Knee Safety.

videos.description:
"Are cross-back lunges bad for your knees?"

I get this question all the time.

The answer isn't a simple yes or no.

Your knees aren't designed to only move forward and backward—they also allow for a small amount of rotation. The key word is small.

That's why cross-back (curtsy) lunges can be a great exercise... as long as you don't exaggerate the crossover.

Instead of stepping way behind your front leg, think about stepping just slightly past the midline. You'll still challenge your glutes, quads, and hip stability without putting unnecessary stress on the knee.

A good rule of thumb:

✅ Slight crossover
❌ Huge crossover

If an exercise consistently causes pain, it's your body's way of telling you something needs to change. NOW, DO IT!!

Have you ever tried cross-back lunges?
.
.
.
#Fitness #LegDay #Lunges #CurtsyLunge #KneeHealth #StrengthTraining #WorkoutTips #ExerciseScience #PersonalTrainer #TrainingTall #Mobility #FunctionalFitness #GymTips #FitnessEducation #HealthyMovement

Is it SAFE for your knee to move side to side when doing Cross-Back or Curtsy Lunges?

The short answer is YES! That’s because the knee does more than just extend and bend the leg. The ligaments within the knee structure allow for SLIGHT rotation of the knee joint!

Key word being SLIGHT! Which basically means that we don’t want to cross back too far to the side!

A good cue to remember is to step “JUST PASS” the midline of the front foot when you cross over - that’s it!

This allows you to keep good knee alignment and build strength in the quads, glutes, and connective tissue that supports that slight rotation!

If this is PAINFUL, you’re doing too much! Either stepping too far to the side or not regressing enough.

Don’t just default to using dumbbells. Try body weight only! Still feeling pain? Regress to holding onto chair or TRX straps to offset some of your weight into your arms. This should be PAIN-FREE, but still challenging!

You’re not too weak to do this! You just need to stop letting your ego get in the way and realize that you can regress while STILL having time to build up strength… life is long and you’ve got time!

But we gotta do it RIGHT and not get hurt!! Now, do it!

If you’re “feeling it in your low back” during deadlifts, I’ve got 2 things to keep in mind to help you feel it less in your back and more in your glutes and hamstrings!

Tip 1 is to make sure you’re keeping the weights as CLOSE TO YOU as you can! Think of it as “shaving your legs” with the dumbbells! Every inch away from your legs the weights go, the more you’re going to feel it in your lower back!

Tip 2 is to BEND YOUR KNEES MORE! When you bend your knees more, it gives you room to scoot your booty back more so you can keep a neutral spine!

If you ARE really flexible though, keep just a little knee bend and think “butt back” to keep you from rounding!

These two tips should help you feel deadlifts a lot less in your lower back and more where you SHOULD be feeling them work!

⚠️ DOES IT HURT TO RUN??

If it does, you’re probably OVER-STRIDING! And this happens when we try to push off of our back foot when we run!

If you push off of your back foot each stride, you have NO CHOICE but to slam out in front of you… which slows you down and puts a ton of negative impact on your joints! It’s simple BAD FORM!!

How SHOULD you run then??

STEP 1: find your pose. This means “pull” your foot up under you. With as little effort as possible!! NOT a knee drive. NOT a butt kick. And NOTHING NUTTY!!! Just a light “pull” of your foot.

STEP 2: Switch your feet. Pull, and switch… back and forth! Again, with as little effort as possible!!

STEP 3: FALL forward with gravity as you switch your feet! Don’t hinge at your hips! Let your WHOLE BODY fall forward as you switch your pull!

THAT IS LITERALLY RUNNING.

This works at 1 mph… 4 mph… 10 mph… 15 mph! It’s all the same!!

Keep this in mind to TRULY elevate your running form and keep you efficient and injury free!

videos.description:
🔥 FAST Sprints on the rower require SPECIAL technique!

This is NOT the technique you’d use for any row longer than 2 minutes max! These tips are focused on peaking power for 10-30ish second sprints primarily!

🔥 Tip 1: don’t bend your legs up all the way!

✅ Focus on heels down, with about a 90 degree leg bend!

🔥 Tip 2: focus on MORE lean at the front!

✅ Peak power comes from the hip swing after the leg drive. Without a lot of lean forward, you’re gonna miss out on power! Think “11 to 1 o’clock” with your body!

🔥 Tip 3: don’t fall off the seat!

✅ Apply your force ONLY horizontally and try to “sit heavy” in the seat!

💪 Combine these tips with aggression and a high stroke rate, and you’re set to CRUSH any row sprint that comes your way! Now, DO IT!

Coach Austin 🤘

#row #rower #rowing #rowingispassion #rowingmachine #erg #rowingworkout #cardio #sprints #hyrox #crossfit #orangetheoryfitness

How the World Record Rowers SPRINT!

These 3 record holders do the exact same things in order to sprint with as much power as possible.

1. They lean forward a lot at the front of the stroke. Getting your torso forward is what allows you to get POWER in the swing back.

2. They keep their heels down. This allows them to take strokes quickly and keep stroke rate high.

3. They REACH the handle up and into the machine. They don’t try to keep “chest tall” or perfect posture.

4. They full extend their legs and lean back. This makes sure you’re using all your leg and hip swing power.

5. They pull the handle in right below the chest, not the stomach, to get more pull distance each stroke.

6. They keep an ever-so-slight rounding forward of the shoulders in order to help keep the stroke rate as high as possible!

If you’ve never believed me, maybe you can believe them! This is how you SPRINT ON THE ROWER!!

Now, do it!

Coach Austin 🤘
.
.
.
#row #rowing #rower #rowingmachine #erg #rowingrelated #sprint #worldrecord

videos.description:
You were taught how to row like a ROBOT! 🤖 

It’s not about “punching out” the arms, then core, then legs. It’s so robotic, feels awful, and is not sustainable for any row longer than a couple minutes!

Instead of “arms” punching out, try think about “relaxing down and out”... the sequence is still arms first, but its not “ARMS”... do you see what I mean? THIS is how you make the rowing stroke feel smooth, sustainable, and efficient while staying true to the “arms core legs” mantra.

I challenge you to see how smooth you can truly make your rowing stroke feel. Be a bit more relaxed with your sequencing and you’re going to find that it works wonders to keep you strong throughout any row!

What’s THE BEST type of Pushup to help you get better?

It’s DEFINITELY the Hand-Release Push-up! Normal push-ups sometimes just won’t cut it.. especially when it cuts our range of motion short and puts our shoulders in a strenuous position!

If you TRULY want to get better at push-ups, you gotta start lifting your hands off of the ground! This means that you lower down as SLOWLY as you can, FULLY lay down, then lift your hands off of the ground, then set them back down before pushing back up!

But when you do, you’ll REALLY get the most out of your pushups!

Give this a shot and watch your push up strength really go up over time!! 💪

SHOULD YOUR HEELS LIFT WHEN YOU ROW?
The Olympic rowers in this video will show you the truth…

The short answer is: yes for the most part!

❌You DO NOT lift your heels if you’re sprinting for 1 minute or less!
❌ You DO NOT lift your heels if you have a large midsection or you’re pregnant!

✅ You DO lift your heels at all other times AS LONG as you can keep a forward body lean every stroke!

✅ You DO lift your heels if the row is longer than 1 minute and you want to be as efficient and long each stroke as possible!

Should your heels lift when you row? 🤔

You’ll see plenty of Olympic rowers lifting their heels at the front of the stroke—but that doesn’t mean everyone needs to do it.

For most people, the bigger priority is maintaining a strong forward body angle.

Think:

🕚 Lean forward toward 11 o’clock
🕐 Swing back toward 1 o’clock

If bending your knees farther causes your torso to become vertical, you’re losing the body swing that helps make the stroke powerful.

Don’t chase extra compression at the expense of good positioning!

title: Here’s EXACTLY how to PR your 200m row
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: Here’s EXACTLY how to PR your 200m row.

videos.description:
Here’s EXACTLY how to PR your 200m row!

This is the ONLY TIME you should be consciously changing your rowing form from the usual “long and strong” form!

A 200m row is so short that you are better off taking more strokes that are shorter and quicker rather than longer, stronger strokes. There’s just not enough time and we need big power FAST!

How do you do this? You keep your heels down and LEAN A LOT!

If you do not lean forward enough, your heels will lift, but they will NEVER lift if you lean forward enough! From there, it’s the same stroke sequence…

Push, swing, pull… big leg push, big swing and lay back! Then a big lean forward at the front again and repeat!!

Do this FAST by pretending you’re stepping on a thumbtack (or lego) at the front of each stroke!

Do this and you’ll PR. Don’t do this if you want to have a slow 200m sprint 🤷‍♂️ The choice is yours.

title: How much should you bend your knees during a dumbbell deadlift
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: How much should you bend your knees during a dumbbell deadlift.

videos.description:
How much should you bend your knees during a dumbbell deadlift?

The problem a lot of folks find is that the cue “a slight knee bend” ends up forcing a rounded spine position simply because of a lack of flexible hamstrings.

If you’re not very flexible, a “slight knee bend” isn’t enough to help you fully hinge over with a full range of motion!

The goal is to get your torso parallel to the ground while keeping a neutral spine position. So, if you’re not very flexible, you need to bend your knees MORE in order to achieve that! The amount of bend will simply vary from person to person - because we all have different levels of flexibility!

The main takeaway is to ALWAYS think “butt back” in order to keep the neutral spine position! Never “reach down”! And when you find the knee bend that works for you and your flexibility, you’ll feel more confident and get better results from this exercise!

Give those tips a try! Hope it helps! Now, DO IT!

title: How to NOT DIE During Inclines & Hills
summary: Reviews setup, common faults, and practical modifications for this topic: How to NOT DIE During Inclines & Hills.

videos.description:
How to NOT DIE During Inclines & Hills…

You want to AVOID “stepping out” or stepping “forward”. This is UNFORTUNATELY how most people run by default due to shoes that have big squishy heels on them. The simple fact is that running this way makes hills WAY HARDER and it’s way more impactful on your joints!!

If you want to run up inclines with less pain and less effort, practice “pose” running!

First, find your pose by pulling your foot up and under you. Don’t knee drive your leg and don’t try to kick your glutes… just simply pull your foot up.

Then, practice picking the other foot up. Notice how the first foot NATURALLY falls down and you don’t have to think about it…. Now, practice switching back and forth. This is running in place!!

Now, all you have to do, is allow gravity to help propel you forward by “falling” forward. By falling forward WHILE you switch your feet, you’re running, and especially when it comes to running hills and inclines, you’re going to be way more efficient!

This stuff take practice AS ANY EXERCISE SKILL SHOULD… but if you don’t actively work on this, you’ll never get better and inclines will ALWAYS SUCK.

My advice? Slow your speeds down to practice this form! You’ve got your whole life to go fast… so don’t let bad form prevent you from reaching your fullest potential!

Love always,

title: How to RUN Without Knee/Hip/Ankle Pain
summary: Reviews setup, common faults, and practical modifications for this topic: How to RUN Without Knee/Hip/Ankle Pain.

videos.description:
⚠️ How to Run Without Knee/Hip/Ankle Pain!

First off, did anyone ever teach you how to run?? For 99% of people, the answer is no! And YES, there is TECHNIQUE to running just like with rowing, cycling, lifting weights, and… EVERYTHING regarding exercise!!

The source of most pain from running comes from crappy form that results from super supportive and squishy shoes! These shoes allow us to run like crap for a while and develop bad habits!

The main bad habit being: striding “out in front of you” and striking down with your heels every step! Ever try standing and jumping and landing on your heels? YOOOOOUUUUCHH!!

But we also don’t want to try to “land on the toes”! This is JUST AS BAD!!

The solution? Learning to run. Here’s the steps:

1️⃣ Find your “pose”. That happens when you simply pull your foot under you with as little effort as possible.

2️⃣ Switch to your other foot and find your pose there. Practice switching back and forth with as LITTLE EFFORT as possible.

3️⃣ Fall with gravity while doing the pose switch.

Those are literally the 3 steps. And with enough practice, it’ll feel more natural. You can literally start doing this at 1 mph and build up to ANY speed! When you go faster, you’ll NATURALLY pull your feet higher and won’t have to think about it!

Were you good at weights the first time you lifted? Were you good at rowing the first time? Were you good AT ANYTHING the first time you tried?? Of course you weren’t. And this is no different. Be patient and practice!

Love always,

The reason why you can’t get the heavy weights overhead is because you’re trying to lift the weight up with your arm too much!!

The Snatch is NOT about using your arm to lift the weight overhead. The arm is just the GUIDE.

Instead, think of the Snatch as a JUMP and ZIP! Literally squat down, hinge back slightly, and JUMP up by driving your quads!

Once you practice and master the “jump and zip”, you’ll be bringing weights overhead that you never thought were possible!

title: I just KNOW you’re getting WRECKED by inclines when running
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: I just KNOW you’re getting WRECKED by inclines when running.

videos.description:
I just KNOW you’re getting WRECKED by inclines when running…

And it’s because you need to work on your running form!

The thing with inclines, is that they REALLY bring your running form errors to light! 

The biggest running form mistake? Trying to “push off” of the back leg or “step forward” with each stride. Both of these things will make you SLOWER in any sort of endurance focused run! That’s because whether you step forward OR push off, you’re going to be getting your leg way out in front of you. And you ONLY move FORWARD when your legs get under, then behind you!

When your leg is in front, you can’t move forward. You need to get your feet to land underneath you! This will come from practicing the Pose Method: pull, switch, and fall!

“Pulling” your feet up does NOT mean you try to drive your knee up or kick your butt. JUST. PULL. Pull your foot up under you!

Practice doing this while switching back forth between feet as quickly, and with as little effort as you can. When you combine this with a “fall forward”, you’re running!

When you fall forward, pretend you’re being pulled up with a string attached to your head! This will prevent you from hinging forward from your hips and will allow gravity to move you forward as pull and switch your feet!

This stuff takes A TON OF PRACTICE. And you have to UN-CONDITION YOURSELF from the crappy form you’ve developed ever since you started playing around in your Nikes/Sketchers/Vans/Converse etc since you were 5 years old. Those shoes that provide cushion and support CONDITIONED you to BAD FORM!

It’s time to undo it all by dropping your ego, slowing your speeds down, and practicing!

This will help you prevent injuries and work through inclines with more confidence! Hope this helps!

videos.description:
If you’re bad at pushups and want to get better, start at the BOTTOM!

Most of us default to starting pushups at the “top” of the movement. This can work for some, but for a lot of folks who can’t crank out a bunch of pushups (or even 1 full pushup without knee assistance), starting at the top of the movement might not be the best idea.

If you start by lying on the floor, you actually give yourself a fighting chance to have great form and a full range of motion each rep!

The key thing here is make sure that you place your hands LOWER than the line of your shoulders! If your hands are too high, you’re going increase your chance of a STRAIN IN YOUR SHOULDERS and probably develop shoulder issues over time…

Proper pushupss require your elbows to guide “back” rather than “out”! That’s why starting on the floor is so great… you can place your hands BELOW the line of the shoulders, which naturally puts your elbows in the correct place.

From there, use your knees to help you out if you need to. You can even regress to a bench, with the same type of start, and build up to your knees over time.

If you’re working on pushups without your knees, this is still a GREAT place to start, because again, it emphasizes PROPER form, and prevents you from doing “ego reps”.

Start your pushups from the bottom rather than the top to help get your pushups to the next level!

Love always,

title: Incline Running Form
summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Incline Running Form.

videos.description:
Whether it’s the Orange Everest Challenge or any other incline-focused treadmill routine, you gotta face reality…

Inclines are TOUGH! And if you struggle to keep any sort of jog or run at any incline over 10%, it’s usually because of your form! Inclines FORCE us to think about our form, because they prevent overstriding!

Over-striding happens when we’re thinking about “stepping forward” with each stride! This is WRONG!! And it will always slow you down…

On the treadmill especially, we can think of our running as “falling while pulling”. Essentially, all we have to do is get our feet off of the ground, fall forward from our hips, and let gravity do the rest!

Lifting off our feet gets us into our “pose position”. Find your “pose” by simply pulling your foot up. Not butt kicking, not knee driving, just pulling it up under you with minimal effort.

Now, simply switch and do the same thing on the alternate foot. Keep switching, and you’re now “running in place”. Now, fall forward from your hips (not your torso), and you’ll be running forward!

You’ll find that inclines become A LOT more manageable when you give this some practice - but it’s gonna take some work!! Do your best!!

Coach Austin 🤘

title: KNEE PAIN DURING LUNGES

videos.description:
🚨KNEE PAIN DURING LUNGES?🚨

If forward lunges make your cringe for your knees, try these tips:

🦵 Step BIGGER – Most people don’t step far enough, which causes that dreaded knee pain. A longer step = less knee shear = happier joints.

⬇️ Drop the BACK knee – Not the front. This helps control the motion and keeps things pain-free. Don’t get it twisted, though! Knees over toes is fine if it’s on purpose. But for sensitive knees, focus on more action from the back knee rather than the front!

💥 Ditch the weights – If you’re hurting, your body is waving a red flag. Start with bodyweight and rebuild smarter!

💪 Use support if bodyweight isn’t enough – TRX handles, a chair, or a bench can help unload your legs into your arms more and help you build confidence.

🧠 Instead of saying “I can’t”, ask “How can I?”
You’ve got your whole life to get stronger, baby! Let’s reverse-engineer it and make it work FOR YOU. 👊🔥

title: Knees-Over-Toes Squat Guidance
summary: Explains setup, regressions, and safety considerations for Knees-Over-Toes Squat Guidance.

videos.description:
Never let your knees go over your toes when you squat…

How many times have you heard that??

If you’re trying to keep your knees from going over your toes to “protect” your knees, you’re probably doing more long-term harm because you’re essentially training your body to not let it be OKAY for your knees to go over your toes?

But should it be okay? YES! Because of natural motions like jumping & going down stairs, our bodies were DESIGNED to have our knees go over our toes!

The key is to regress squats as FAR BACK AS YOU NEED TO in order to squat knees over toes pain-free.

That means no weights, and not even bodyweight if that hurts… use assistance to shift some of your weight into your upper body, such as TRX to offset up to 99.99% of your bodyweight.

There IS a pain-free level you can start with… and then you have your entire life to build up and get strong! We just need to drop our ego, and regress in order to BUILD down the line!

Let’s get back to training our body to have increased ABILITY, rather than try to limit it - especially as we get older!

Love always,

title: Lateral Lunge Technique Tips

videos.description:
After 12 years as a personal trainer…

I can confidently say that I still despise Lateral Lunges!

Not because they’re bad for you… they’re actually one of the BEST leg exercises in my opinion!

But because of how HARD they are!! Simply such an uncomfortable and challenging exercise.. but I’ve got some tips for you!

First, lighten the load. There is no need to load up super heavy on this exercise unless you have MASTERED the movement and have the mobility and strength to support big dumbbells.

Try 1 weight held goblet-style rather than 2 weights at your sides to reduce the load and help you keep more upright - rather than collapsing down!

Unlike a squat, where the focus is sitting your hips “back and down”, on the Lateral Lunges, focus more on simply “bending the knee”! This is a MUCH better way to think about the movement and will help you get a bigger stretch on your inner thighs while helping you get deeper in the lunge!

This move is TRULY one of the toughest legs exercises out there! But you’ve got this! Give it your best shot… now, do it! 💪

title: Leg-Raise Back-Pain Modification
summary: Explains setup, regressions, and safety considerations for Leg-Raise Back-Pain Modification.

videos.description:
Do you put your “hands under” yourself when you do Leg Raises?

A lot of people do this because leg raises bother their lower back! Instead of this, try to LIFT your head, neck, and shoulders off of the ground and “crunch up” before you start your reps!

This will active your entire midsection AND eliminate any discomfort you might feel in your lower back from the exercise!

It’s a good way to also train your neck muscles a bit, too! If you feel your neck tense up, that means it’s working!! The neck has muscles just like the rest of your body and this is an easy way to lightly train it while doing core work, too!

If you haven’t tried this before, give it a shot! It’s my go-to for leg raises EVERY TIME now!

Is this the ONLY way to modify the exercise? Not at all! But I find that it’s the simplest way to change it up, “feel it more”, and keep you safe!

videos.description:
I see those sneaky hands…

Hands under your booty during Leg Raises? We subconsciously do this because we don’t have the strength to keep a neutral spine as we lower our legs down, which makes our back arch excessively and creates low back pain!

One solution is to reduce the range of motion until you cant keep your spine neutral - SURE!

BUT another option is to CRUNCH UP your head, beck and shoulders, and THEN do the leg raises! This gets more of your midsection involved and virtually eliminates any back pain!

Just try to think about your hips “scooping” as you do your reps rather than just “lifting your legs”!

Give this variation a try if you haven’t already and thank me later!!

title: Loaded Stretch in Strength Training

videos.description:
What you’re doing with your weight training probably isn’t helping you see long lasting results…

If you’re just focusing on “completing your reps”, you’re probably missing out on one of the most important aspects of weight training: the loaded stretch on your muscles in the most lengthened positions of the exercise!

Basically, the more STRETCH you can get on the muscles each rep, the better results you’ll see! 

It’s not about just “doing your reps”! A philosophy like that will have you most likely doing your reps more rushed and with less focus on a full range of motion. 

Sometimes, our ego gets in the way too. We end up going heavier to show off, but again, cut the most important part of the lift short by not focusing on a big stretch each rep!!

If you’ve been in a plateau, it might be time to start focusing less on your reps and more about the loaded stretch you can get each rep! You might even need LESS WEIGHT!!

Not only is this stretch philosophy great for muscle gains, but it helps us build flexibility and joint strength, too!! Nothing but wins!! But you still gotta do it!!

Now, do it!!

title: Lunge Depth and Pain-Free Regressions
summary: Covers setup, common faults, and practical modifications for Lunge Depth and Pain-Free Regressions.

videos.description:
You’re probably not going low enough with lunges…

The gold standard is dropping your back knee just a little bit above touching the ground! If you’re going any shallower than that, you’re missing out and cheating the reps!

However, going that low can cause PAIN for a lot of folks.

The solution? Use a lighter weight. If that’s too much, you need to go full body weight! And if THAT is still causing pain, it’s time to grab some TRX suspension straps!!

The TRX allow you to offset up to 99% of your body weight into your arms to make it easier on your legs - as much as you need to for pain-free movement!

We NEVER want to work through pain… but your joints will ONLY get stronger when you train their full range at your current regression level. You have your ENTIRE LIFE to build up and get strong, but you have to give yourself a chance by dropping your ego, lightening the load, and doing it RIGHT!

Hope this can resonate!

Love always,

title: Pull-Up Progression
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: Pull-Up Progression.

videos.description:
Can’t Do a Pull-Up? Here’s the formula…

1️⃣ Start off with Bar Hangs! Sounds too easy, I know, but THIS is the foundation of building pull-up strength! Literally just hanging!

2️⃣ After some weeks of practice, you move on to Scapular Retractions! This is where you start to really use your “pull-up muscles”, focusing on pulling your shoulder blades down, holding, and building strength in that contracted position!

3️⃣ Then, you move into Eccentric Pull-ups! This means using a chair/bench/something to get yourself to the top of the pull-up, holding your scapular retraction, then SLOWLY lowering down! You WILL build strength by controlling the way down! (Aka the eccentric).

4️⃣ Then, it’s time for assisted pull-ups! Use a bench/chair/something to put your leg on, then use as little/much effort in the leg as you need to to “get up” for the pull-up, then, release the leg and work on your eccentric on the way down!

5️⃣ After a few months of all of this work, you’ll be ready to start cranking out your first pull-up! This strength takes A LOT of time and patience, so don’t try to rush the process!

And of course, there are other ways to work towards pull-ups, but I like this strategy the most! What do you think!? Can you do a pull-up??

videos.description:
Don’t fall into the trap of defaulting to “no knees needed” pushups if you can’t get the full range!!

You’re letting your precious ego get in the way from you actually getting RESULTS!

Instead, keep in mind these regressions:

1. Knees on the ground. Remember to squeeze your butt forward, brace your abs, and aim diagonally down to the bench TOUCHING your chest!

2. No-Knee Eccentrics! These are the bridge between knees and “no knee” pushups! Keep your knees off of the ground for the eccentric (lowering phase), which is where your body is strongest. TOUCH your chest, then place your knees down to push yourself back to the top! Make sure you go slow on the way down to get the most out of this variation!

You have your ENTIRE LIFE to get “good” at pushups! But you’ll never get there if all you do is half-range BS pushups!! So, dial back, and the let the gains begin! 💪 Now, do it!

Reality check: You’re not getting better at pushups because you’re TOO SCARED to regress…

Getting good at pushups comes from MASTERING every single regression.

That is going to take a hit to your ego… because the fitness world has deemed pushups to be this thing that everyone should just be able to do… that’s HORRENDOUSLY false, by the way.

Start by mastering Bench Pushups. And by mastery, we’re talking FULL RANGE touching your chest to the bench EVERY REP. When you can string together consistent sets of 10 reps at least, you’re ready for Level 2.

Level 2 is the knee pushup. Knees on the ground, and aiming diagonally down and forward, TOUCHING YOUR CHEST, then pushing up and back. One again, work your way up to nailing 3+ sets of 10 reps with this level before moving on.

Level 3 is the HYBRID pushup, which I like to think of as “knees on, knees off”. You start by going down SLOWLY without your knees on the ground, to a 3 second count. Touch your chest, then put your knees ON the ground, then push back up and repeat.

When you get good at those, eventually you’ll be able to TRULY knock out pushups without your knees, with QUALITY form and NO EGO!

This is what it takes. Good pushups are hard to do. And getting strong at pushups is a long and strenuous journey. But the good news is you have your whole life to GET GOOD. But it starts with doing things RIGHT!

Love always,

title: Push-Swing-Pull Rowing Sequence
summary: Explains the push-swing-pull sequence, emphasizing leg drive before the torso swing and arm pull.

videos.description:
Rowing cardio = PUSH, not pull…

When you lift weights and “row”, you’re using your back and arm muscles to PULL the weight- as you should!

But in the CARDIO version of rowing, you’re using your entire body! That means you gotta use your LEGS if you want to get the most out of the rowing stroke!

And that means you have to PUSH away using your legs BEFORE you pull your arms at the end!

The # 1 mistake people make is “pulling” the start of the stroke - and it’s totally destroying your rowing capability! Do your best to remember to PUSH instead of pull, to start every stroke! 👍

Your rowing form is BAD because you’re trying to “pull” the stroke! You only PULL when you row when you’re doing bodybuilding training on weighted machines.

Rowing machines simulate the SPORT of ROWING, which is totally different than “pull rowing”!

The rowing stroke is a PUSH! That’s how you want to initiate every stroke.

Think of the full stroke as a “push, swing, pull”! PUSH your legs first, then SWING the hips/body back, then PULL the arms in!

But that initial starting PUSH is sooo important! Without it, you have no power in the SWING!

So do your best to be extra mindful to hold your torso forward as you PUSH instead of pull, then swing, then pull! Do this and your rowing performance is gonna go through the roof!!

title: Reading the Rowing Force Curve
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: Reading the Rowing Force Curve.

videos.description:
💥 The Force Curve!

This handy graph can help you better understand where your force is being distributed each stroke!

There are plenty of examples to share for this, but here are the 3 I chose, all revolving around rowing at a steady pace between 22-25 SPM. These graphs and what’s ideal would look different for sprints, just FYI!

Example 1 shows what the curve looks like when you overuse your arms in the stroke. You see a big peak/spike happen towards the end of the line during the arm pull. A tell-all sign that you’re putting too much effort into your arms compared to your legs and hips!

Example 2 shows an “early layback”, which is when you negate the entire hip swing portion of the rowing stroke and only rely on the leg drive and arm pull. This is evidenced by a steady climbing-upwards with it peaking towards the back half of the stroke!

Example 3 shows us what a good proper stroke graph should be at this steady rate, a smooth hill with a peak that’s more towards the middle of the stroke - the point right after the leg drive and your torso swings through vertical!

When you’re rowing steady, aim for this “smooth hill” graph to show that you’re getting proper power distribution from your body efficiently each stroke! 💪

Wanna see more examples? 🤔

Coach Austin 🤘

title: Row Form Checklist
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: Row Form Checklist.

videos.description:
EASY ROW FORM CHECKLIST:

At the END (aka “finish”) of the rowing stroke, make sure:

1. Your elbows are both OUT and BACK with wrists flat.

2. The handle is pulled right below the chest (below the bra strap).

3. Your shoulders are relaxed and eyes and head are forward.

4. Your body is leaned back at a 1 o clock angle.

On the RETURN of the stroke to come up for the next stroke, make sure:

1. You RELAX your arms down and out over your knees (don’t punch out!)

2. As you bend your knees, lean forward to 11 o clock

3. Compress your legs as much as you can while maintaining 11 o clock.

4. Extend your arms fully straight and lift your hands ever-so-slightly to eliminate slack when you take the stroke.

As you TAKE the stroke:

1. Drive your legs down while HOLDING your 11 o clock position (don’t lean as you push your legs).

2. SWING back as your legs near full straightening.

3. Pull the arms in at the very end using the momentum generated before!

There ya go! Do you hit all of these check boxes?? Hope it helps you with your rowing!

Love always,

Coach Austin 🤘

videos.description:
❌ IT’S NOT A “RESISTANCE” SETTING!

That dial on the side of the @concept2inc RowErg? It’s called the “damper setting”!

💨 It controls how much air goes into the system as you row!

🔟 When the dial is up at 10, it’s allowing MORE air to flow, which slows down the fan faster! This can make the start of each stroke “feel heavier”.

1️⃣ When the dial is at 1, it’s allowing LESS air to flow, which keeps the fan spinning for longer. This can make the start of each stroke feel more “light and airy”!

❌ However, neither setting determines HOW HARD THE WORKOUT WILL BE!!

✅ The challenge of a rowing workout is based on how much EFFORT you put into each stroke. You can row LIGHTLY at damper 10 and feel nothing.. or you can row as HARD AS POSSIBLE at damper 1 and be cooked in a couple minutes!! 🔥

👍 That’s why setting 3-5 works for most people, for most workouts! Gives you a good balance with how fast the fan slows down and allows you to row hard without making each stroke super heavy feeling!

Who woulda thought!! Now ya know!! 😃 🤘 Questions? Let me know!

As you can see in this video, whether the resistance setting (actually called ‘the damper’) is set to 1 or 10, you can STILL achieve the same split/500m.

Granted, it definitely does FEEL LIGHTER at a lower damper setting! It was a bit more difficult to find a rhythm with it, but that’s because I’m 6ft8 and 225 pounds! If you’re shorter and smaller, you’ll have a bit of an easier time with a lower damper as it will allow you rely more on stroke rate than pure power per stroke!

The point is, just because the “resistance” is lower, doesn’t mean your workout is objectively easier or you can’t go as hard!

✅ You need to find a damper setting that works for you, which for most is in the 3-6 range on the dial! But remember that your workout on the rower is mainly determined by how HARD you take your strokes!

So, if rowing feels too easy, drive back HARDER each stroke - and don’t just crank the damper setting up to 10! 😉

title: Rower Handle Path
summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Rower Handle Path.

videos.description:
Rowing isn’t what you think it is.

The “way to row” is a lot more dynamic than it might seem!

We do NOT want to think about the handle moving in a straight line in and out of the rower. This makes the motion very robotic and can tire out muscles that aren’t helpful for efficient rowing.

We also do NOT want to “swirl” or “swoosh” the handle as if you’re taking your oars in and out of the water. This leads to too much motion and inefficiency and can lead to chaos at higher stroke rates!

Both are wrong! But the RIGHT way to row involves a combination of both.

On the return, you want to RELAX your arms and shoulders to allow the handle to tap down close to your thighs.

Once you pass the knees, the handle starts to track UP into a lifted position at the catch (front) position!

On the drive, the handle drives back fairly straight, but in a slightly diagonal motion to maximize stroke distance! And then, the process repeats!

Once you can start implementing this into your rowing, you’ll feel just how fluid, efficient, and strong your rowing can be! Now, DO IT!

title: Rower Handle Path and Chain Connection

videos.description:
Not enough people realize how MASSIVE of a mistake this is…

On the @concept2inc (and pretty much every rowing machine, water rower etc)- you’ve gotta understand that the chain CONNECTS during the stroke sequence at a SLIGHT DIAGONAL angle!

It is not “straight in and out of the machine”. Seriously… go film yourself rowing and you will see EVERY TIME the chain snaps up slightly.

Every inch of the drive you take before the “snap up” is WASTED because you have little to no connection when the chain isn’t slightly diagonally pulled.

While this example in the video might be exaggerated, carrying your hands low is taking most of the efficiency out of your rowing stroke.

❌ The answer is NOT to “scoop” the handle to lift the hands! This is unsustainable at high stroke rates.

✅ Instead, try this drill. Pause at the knees with the handle low to your thighs, then slowly “trickle” aka lift your hands up up up… it’s a SUBTLE movement. Then, drive back with your hands lifted high and notice INSTANTLY how much stronger and connected your stroke feels.

Massive difference. That handle path takes some practice to nail down, but once you get it, you’ll feel connected from start to finish every stroke! 💪

Happy rowing! 🚣‍♂️

Slowing down the return to a 2-3 second count really helps you to practice proper form sequencing and gives the monitor a chance to run out some extra meters every stroke!

Start taking your time on the way back up, and drive back with as much force as you can, and you’ll start to enjoy rowing A LOT MORE!

title: Rower Sitting Position and Back Safety

videos.description:
DON’T USE THE ROWER! IT’S BAD FOR YOUR BACK!!

How many times have you hear that before?

The thing is.. a lot of lower back injuries DO happen on the rower. But the good news is that those injuries are TOTALLY preventable!

In fact most rowing back pain and injuries occurs because of how you SIT on the seat! If you sit on the middle of your butt, when you reach forward to the front of the stroke, your lower back unintentionally rounds, and that’s usually what causes a back strain!

Instead, try to “sit on your junk” 🥜! A funny phrase I like to use to describe the action of tilting forward on your hips, trying to sit more on your hamstrings than your a$$, to help you untuck your lower back and keep it in a neutral spine position at the front of each stroke!

If you’re sitting on YOUR NICE CUSHY BUM, you’re messing up!!

When you row, if you sit where it’s the most comfy, you’re most likely tucking your pelvis underneath you, which is going to round your lower back as you row.
 When your lower back is rounded, you’re just ASKING for a low back strain when using the rowing machine. AND it will prevent you from getting maximum length in your stroke, and the most power out of your body SWING after you push your legs.

And ALL YOU HAVE TO DO TO FIX THIS, is take 2 SECONDS to try to “untuck your lower back” by sitting more on your HAMSTRINGS than your glutes!

Sure, it isn’t as comfortable, but it’s a SAFER and STRONGER position and a NON-NEGOTIABLE if you want to row well and pain-free!

Next time you sit down to row, YOU BETTER NOT “JUST SIT”! Take those couple seconds to sit more on your hamstrings and untuck your lower back, and you’re going to be ready to crush ANY ROW that comes your way!!

A CLASSIC example of “good form” that’s actually BAD!

title: Rowing Catch Body Position

videos.description:
If you want to level up your rowing power, you’ve gotta master the front end body position with the rowing stroke!

This position tends to be one of the most difficult to get right when looking at the entire rowing stroke - and even small mistakes can cost you A LOT of power!

This most important aspect of a good front catch position on the rower is to make sure your torso angles forward at a 1 o’clock position.
 A LOT of people make the mistake of bending the legs too much, with makes it nearly impossible to get the proper lean forward. This usually results in a more “vertical torso”. And if your torso is vertical, you won’t get much power in your layback with each stroke!

To help ensure you get the proper lean forward, I highly encourage you to bend your legs less. This gives you more room to lean in! Try thinking “heels down, lean more” to help with this!

The pro rowers are able to bend their legs all the way while still getting the proper lean, and you can do that too if you have the flexibility and awareness to do so.

But for most, just start with less leg bend to help with more lean!

From there, you know the drill: Push, swing, pull!

title: Rowing Leg Drive Not Arm Pull
summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Rowing Leg Drive Not Arm Pull.

videos.description:
⚠️ If you want MORE meters for FREE when rowing, you gotta stop pulling each stroke.

Rowing is a pull, right? In most contexts, YES. But in the contexts of rowing on a ROWING MACHINE, the stroke is very much NOT a pull!

It’s a PUSH. Every stroke starts with a leg push. And while many have HEARD that before, most still struggle to execute the leg push properly. 

Most end up with a sort of “push legs AND pull arms at the same time”-hybrid type of movement! I personally was guilty of this for YEARS when I was rowing in college.

But a true rowing PUSH with the legs means that your torso stays LEANED forward for the first half of the rowing stroke. If you lean back AT ALL during the leg push, you miss out on the power of the hip swing.

But if you swing AFTER a leg push and THEN pull, that’s where the magic happens! I like to think of it as “earning the right to pull” each stroke. You only earn it if you push, then swing first!

I hope that makes sense… this takes some SERIOUS practice and intention. But it will pay off for you in the long run! Let me know your thoughts…

title: Rowing Machine vs Racing Shell Handle Path

Everyone THINKS they know how to row because of their CrossFit or Orangetheory coach…

But training on the erg (aka the rowing machine) is A LOT different than rowing in a racing shell…

The dynamic path the handle should take while erging relaxes your shoulders, tapping your arms “down and out” followed by a slow lift up to the catch position, from where you then drive back and pull into the chest.

This is NOT what you see in a rowing boat. Most finish positions end with the oar handle close to the lap, and the angle of the handle path is a “high to low” path due to the angular motion of the rowing oar through water.

Why don’t the pros on the U23 German women’s team and GB men’s team (in these video example) row on the machines like they would on the water? Because they are training their FITNESS on the ergs and training their SKILLS on the water.

Why would you row like you’re on a boat if you’re not on a boat where the dynamics and environment are completely different? It’s all about context!

Also, stop punching your arms out when you row because that’s making you slower! 😃

title: Rowing Modifications for Larger Midsections
summary: Covers setup, common faults, and practical modifications for Rowing Modifications for Larger Midsections.

videos.description:
The idea here is to manage having a larger midsection while still being able to achieve the same LEAN at the front of each stroke that you would get if you didn’t have a large midsection.

Most that are heavier tend to feel like they’re getting crushed when they try to lean in - so how do we fix it?

1. Loosen the foot straps. This allows you to turn your feet out, and therefore push your knees out instead of keeping them together. And no, this is not bad for your knees.

2. Stop bending your legs all the way up. Keep your heels down and only bend to ~90 degrees in your legs. This will give you room to lean without hurting your lower back.

And you’re good to go! Push, swing, pull. Same sequencing, same stroke technique for the most part! Hope this helps!

- Coach Austin 🤘

If you have a large midsection (pregnant or otherwise), you won’t row optimally if you try to row with traditional rowing form!

You have to modify a couple things if you want to get the most out of every rowing stroke! 👍

First thing is to NOT strap in tight with your feet! Loosen up the foot straps instead and point your toes and knees out slightly!

‼️ PSA ‼️ Rowing with your knees angled out will NOT hurt your knees as long as your toes point out, too!

Second thing to do is to grip the handle with a NARROW grip, rather than as wide as possible!

A narrow grip will allow you to row between your legs, which lets you get the ideal lean forward we want each stroke!

With those two changes in mind, it’s the same PUSH - SWING - PULL sequence you’d normally do! The mechanics stay the same… the setup is what changes!

title: Rowing Stroke Rate and Power
summary: Provides pacing, progression, or workout-planning guidance for this topic: Rowing Stroke Rate and Power.

videos.description:
Burn more calories on the rower by SLOWING DOWN!

For those that aren’t experienced with using a rowing machine properly, they think that faster = more calories.

The “speed” of your rowing, aka the “stroke rate” is simply a measure of the rhythm of how many strokes you’re taking in… NOT HOW HARD YOU ARE TAKING STROKES!

To make rowing burn a lot of calories and actually feel like a good workout, you need to take strokes HARDER, and NOT row “faster”!

Rowing machines generate resistance based on how much EFFORT goes into the drive of each stroke. You could have a stroke rate of 30 strokes per minute, but if you’re not putting EFFORT into each stroke, you’re doing a whole lot of NOTHING! Hence the 700 calories per hour that happens when I just bounce up and down with no actual effort.

By slowing your stroke rate / rhythm down, you can actually get a better workout on the rower because you can focus on your form, but more importantly, putting more EFFORT into each stroke! That’s why you can see that at 20 strokes per minute, I can burn 2 times as many calories because I’m actually TRYING HARD each stroke - even though the rate is lower!

Can you generate even more by rowing hard AND using a high stroke rate? Absolutely! But you can’t row well at a fast stroke rate until you learn how to row well at a low stroke rate, first!

Start rowing SLOW if you ACTUALLY want to start getting in a good workout on the rower! 💪 Questions? Ask them!

title: Running Pose Pull Switch Fall
summary: Explains movement mechanics and practical coaching points for Running Pose Pull Switch Fall.

videos.description:
One of the biggest misconceptions about running is that you should be moving forward by pushing off of your foot each stride.

But if you do this, all it does is make you step further out in front - and you can’t move forward when your leg is out in front of you! Plus it causes you to strike hard on your heel and can increase your risk of developing joint issues in your running journey!

It’s NOT about trying to step forward or “push off”! Instead, focus on finding your runners pose!

This means simply pulling your foot up - not a knee drive or butt kick, just pull your foot up!

Then, pull the other foot up, and practice switching back and forth between your feet with as little effort as possible!

Now all you have to do is use gravity to help you move forward by “falling” forward from your hips while pulling and switching your feet!

Doing this will help you land with your feet under you more, which prevents over-striding that only hurts you and slows you down!

It takes some practice, but it’s worthwhile to practice and build up the technique! Soon you’ll be running pain free and as fast as ever! 💪

The drastic differences in form and effort between 130, 150, and 180 strides per minute really highlight how cadence impacts our running!

At 130, you basically have to jump each step, POUNDING down on your joints just to keep up…

At 150, things get a little better, but you still end up landing your heel way out in front of your body, creating a ton of unnecessary impact.

At 180, the quick cadence of the feet allows the feet to land much closer to your center of mass, allowing you to more effectively use your foot and calf musculature to cushion your landing, resulting in way less impact!

Does that mean 180 is the perfect cadence? Not necessarily, but it does highlight that a higher cadence in general can help reduce intense impact on your joints each stride!

Something to think about… 😉 NOW DO IT!

You’re PROBABLY not as bad at sit-ups as you think you are…

You may just not have realized that the MORE you bend your legs, the HARDER sit-ups are.

videos.description:
9 Out of 10 People Do Step-Ups Wrong!

And that’s because 9 out of 10 people aren’t thinking about WHEN they are switching their feet!

And most end up switching where it feels “natural”, which is on TOP of the bench! But this isn’t ideal..

And that’s because when you switch your feet at the top, you’re working one leg on the way up, and the opposite leg on the way down - robbing your working leg of a full concentric and eccentric contraction! You don’t get a true full rep!!

title: Stop going into the unknown with your TRX Chest Press

videos.description:
Stop going into the unknown with your TRX Chest Press!

If you’re starting this move from the top, you’re guessing your way through the setup — and that’s how form breaks down. Instead, start from the bottom:

✅ Walk yourself forward
✅ Get the handles under your armpits
✅ Elbows out and back
✅ THEN step back and press

Now every rep has a roadmap. You’ll feel more stable, more confident, and get more out of every set. Don’t just “see what happens” — take control from the start and build strength AND confidence on the TRX!

99% make this TRX Mistake...

And that’s trying to start push-ups / chest press at “THE TOP” of the movement!

It seems like the intuitive thing to do, but the tricky thing with TRX is that they are so unstable, it’s hard to gauge exactly how challenging it’s going to be!

And when it comes to building muscle, getting stronger, and staying injury free, we want to maximize a SAFE FULL-RANGE!

And MOST people don’t even come close to the full range of motion on the TRX chest press...

If you instead start the movement “at the bottom”, but walking forward, getting the handles situated under your shoulders, THEN stepping back to load it, and THEN pressing to the top - you’ll be able to safely get the full range while feeling confidently challenged!

It seems strange, I know... but you gotta give it a try if you haven’t before!

You’re going to feel so much more confident in your body, and with every rep, when you START AT THE BOTTOM!

Give it a shot! Now, do it!

Love always,

Coach Austin 🤘
.
.
.
#trx #trxtraining #trxworkout #pushups #chestday #orangetheory #orangetheoryfitness #fitnesstips

The biggest TRX push-up mistake happens before the first rep even begins!

Most people start at the top and then lower themselves without knowing exactly where they’re supposed to stop.

Instead:

1️⃣ Walk forward into the bottom position
2️⃣ Place the handles underneath your shoulders
3️⃣ Step backward until your muscles load
4️⃣ Press yourself up

Now you have a clear target for every repetition—and you can adjust your foot position to make the exercise appropriately challenging.

Start at the bottom. Then load it up! 💪 NOW DO IT!

title: The Rowing Pick Drill
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: The Rowing Pick Drill.

videos.description:
The #1 drill every rowing Olympian has ever done… and why you should do it too!

✨ The Pick Drill ✨

This drill at its core helps you develop the basic sequencing of a proper rowing stroke.

It starts with ~60 seconds of “arms only”. This means only extending your arms out and pulling them in. During this part you should:
✅ Hold your legs flat, quads flexed
✅ Hold your layback, abs braced
✅ Pull in below the chest

The second part is ~60 seconds of “arms + torso”… sometimes called “arms and core”. Same thing.
During this part you should:
✅ Keep your legs flat, quads flexed
✅ Focus on a big hip swing, then pull

Finally, finish the drill by adding in the legs for a full stroke…
At this point, your stroke should feel a lot more purposeful and more efficient!
✅ Try to keep a fluid sequence
✅ Think “push, swing, pull” on the drive

This drill is great for all fitness levels. If you struggle with good rowing form, give this a go as a warmup before your next rowing session!

Coach Austin 🤘
.
.

title: This drill will fix one of the BIGGEST mistakes in your rowing
summary: Reviews key mechanics and actionable movement cues for this topic: This drill will fix one of the BIGGEST mistakes in your rowing.

videos.description:
This drill will fix one of the BIGGEST mistakes in your rowing.

And that mistake is leaning back early. Or “opening up” early with the torso.

I have coached 1000s on rowing form personally, and time and time again, this early lean back is one of the biggest issues preventing folks from maximizing their rowing potential.

Doing the “Legs Only” drill is a great way to fix it. All you have to do is take a few strokes (usually 1 or 2 minutes worth between 16-20 s/m) with ONLY pushing your legs back.

Careful when you do this, you’ll want to lean back. But try not to! The lean in the rowing stroke happens AFTER the legs. Proper power and form comes from pushing the legs first, then right as the legs near full extension, you swing back with your torso and pull in the arms.

If you lean early, there is no power in the swing. But if you can do Legs Only, and then transition to full strokes, you can achieve the power in the swing as you lean AFTER the leg drive!

This takes TONS of practice, but why not give this drill a shot for a minute or two before your next workout to help you improve your form!

Questions? Let me know! And thanks @eltgilmore for the great demo. And thanks @keepitjorganic for the great shirt.

videos.description: Refining the transverse squat! We do a lot of saggital plane movements and even some frontal plane but not too much in the transverse plane.  1. Don’t plant the foot then squat. If you plant the foot then squat. The tranverse plane only worked to get the foot into place, then you are doing a regular squat. Think rotate and squat simultaneously.  2. If the knee collapses inside of the big toe, we get excessive stress on the lateral stabilizers of the base leg knee. Make sure knee tracks 2nd/3rd toe. If the base foot moves, we are taking away from the tranverse plane and getting closer to a transverse lunge vs a squat. Glue that foot in place.  4. Stepping back in-line with the base leg puts excessive rotation at either the knee or hip. Make sure to step back and out. Using your arms to help you up on Sit-ups is NOT CHEATING!

In fact, it’s one of the best tools you can use to help you get stronger at sit-ups if you really struggle with them!

That’s because your arms help you out on the “concentric” phase of the sit-up (the actual sitting up part). THIS is where our muscle strength is at its weakest, and that’s why having the arms to help is a great option!

But that’s because the REAL STRENGTH is going to be gained on the eccentric part of the sit-up (lowering back down from the top). THIS is where our muscles are the STRONGEST, and as long as you lower down slowly and keep tension, you’re going to build a ton of abs strength that will EVENTUALLY make it so you don’t have to sue your arms to get up!

But if you just GIVE UP because you don’t want to use your arms to get you up, you’ll never build the strength! So, use those arms!! Just control the way down, too! 👍 Now, DO IT!
